title: Cache eviction–induced priority inversion and fallback orchestration initiative
creator: Aisha Raman
description: During a multi-region traffic surge on 2026-02-14, we observed cascading latency spikes and partial SLO misses tied to an interaction between the KV cache eviction policy and circuit-breaker hysteresis. The cache eviction logic aggressively expired cold shards in Region-B under memory pressure, which amplified backend load and triggered a cascade of lower-priority requests to preempt priority queues. Circuit breakers in Region-A and Region-B used slightly different hysteresis thresholds and lockout windows; they failed to synchronize during the surge. The combination caused a priority inversion: lower-priority background prep jobs consumed hot CPU/GPU threads while high-priority inference requests timed out and were routed across regions, leading to failover thrash and sustained 99th-percentile latency degradation. This ticket documents the investigation, interim mitigations we ran during the incident, and the multi-step permanent remediation plan and action owners.
timeline: 2026-02-14 09:12 UTC: First latency alert from Synthetic 99th p90 in Region-B (escalated by on-call)
2026-02-14 09:18 UTC: Automated traffic steering moved 18% of sessions to Region-C; some routes experienced long tail errors
2026-02-14 09:27 UTC: Priority-queue saturation noticed; background replication jobs consuming GPU cycles
2026-02-14 09:41 UTC: Ops applied emergency traffic cap for background queues and manually raised eviction TTLs in Region-B
2026-02-14 10:05 UTC: Circuit breakers in Region-A opened briefly then re-closed causing oscillation; failover rollbacks observed
2026-02-14 11:30 UTC: Incident considered mitigated after coordinated shedding and TTL changes; monitoring in steady state by 12:00 UTC
root_cause: Near-simultaneous hot-shard KV cache evictions in Region-B due to an under-tuned memory-pressure eviction policy plus divergent circuit-breaker hysteresis settings between regions. Evictions generated bursty backend recompute and cold-starts that overwhelmed worker pools; priority scheduling allowed lower-priority jobs to occupy GPU resources during the initial shock, producing priority inversion and multi-region failover oscillation.
impact_metrics: SLOs: user-facing generation SLO (p99 latency < 1200ms) breached for 28 minutes (peak p99 = 3.8s)
Error rate: coherent 5xx rate increased from 0.12% to 1.9% during peak
Traffic: cross-region failover spiked cross-region traffic by +42% between Region-A and Region-B
Cost: provisional estimate +18% GPU consumption for the incident hour due to recompute
mitigations_during_incident: Raised KV cache short-TTL threshold and disabled aggressive shard eviction in Region-B (ops@10:41)
Applied emergency rate caps on background/replication jobs via per-tenant route rules (ops@09:50)
Tuned circuit-breaker to longer hysteresis window as temporary stabilization (ops@10:00)
Replayed degraded traffic patterns to synthetic canaries to validate stabilizing changes (SRE@11:00)
permanent_fixes: Consolidate circuit-breaker config into a single cross-region policy with synchronized hysteresis and unified failback logic (owner: Marco Silva, due: 2026-03-14)
Introduce a priority-locking mechanism on GPU worker pools to reserve headroom for high-priority inference pipelines and preempt background tasks (owner: Priya Kulkarni, due: 2026-04-04)
Revise KV cache eviction algorithm to incorporate recency-weighted shard scoring and to support soft-eviction with warmup leases (owner: Carlos Mendes, due: 2026-03-21)
Add a cross-region synthetic that exercises priority inversion scenarios at scale as a gated SLO regression test in CI (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-07)
Create automatic protective shed rules that detect asymmetric eviction events and proactively limit low-priority background load (owner: Marco Silva, due: 2026-03-11)

postmortem_summary: A combination of aggressive shard eviction and unsynchronized circuit-breaker hysteresis created conditions for priority inversion and multi-region failover oscillation. Mitigations stabilized service within three hours. We have a prioritized set of fixes (circuit sync, priority-locking, eviction algorithm changes, and additional canaries) with clear owners and delivery dates to prevent recurrence.
